c.tagline: Spiritual heart of Sikhism — the glowing Golden Temple, langar for all, and Punjab's buttery, generous cuisine.

taxi.fareNote: Autos and taxis rarely use meters; agree the fare before boarding, or book via Uber/Ola for a fixed price. E-rickshaws shuttle the last stretch to the Golden Temple, which is otherwise pedestrianised.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-services emergency number; 108 reaches ambulance services and 100 the police.

avoid.reason: Touts around the Golden Temple; pickpocketing in crowds

hood_desc: The walled old city around the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib), reached via the pedestrianised, Mughal-styled Heritage Street and steps from Jallianwala Bagh and the langar hall. The place to stay if you want to walk to the temple at dawn.
Amritsar's dense traditional bazaar quarter, a warren of markets for Phulkari textiles, jewellery, papad-warian and street food; loud, colourful and central.
A prosperous strip of restaurants, cafes, bars and shops that is the city's main dining-out and evening address, a short drive from the old city.
A planned, upmarket residential district with wide roads, malls (Alpha One / Trilium), hotels and quieter modern comforts on the city's eastern side.

The colonial-era spine running out from the old city, lined with civic buildings, the Ram Bagh gardens and the newer Mall of Amritsar; a convenient, well-connected base between the historic core and the newer town.
lodging: Country Inn & Suites by Radisson Amritsar

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only, and avoid ice from unknown sources.

transit.hours: City buses and shared autos run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; ride apps and e-rickshaws fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Amritsar has no metro or tram. Auto-rickshaws, e-rickshaws and city buses are the main way around; the Golden Temple precinct and Heritage Street are pedestrianised, so the final approach is on foot or by e-rickshaw.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash and are usually negotiated, not metered — agree the price before you board. Booking an auto through Uber or Ola gives a fixed fare.

tip.r: Not customary; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at nicer restaurants is appreciated. There is no tipping at the Golden Temple's free langar.

food.name: Amritsari kulcha
food.desc: Crisp, ghee-drenched flatbread stuffed with spiced potato or paneer, smashed open and served with chole and tangy imli chutney.

places.name: Kesar Da Dhaba
places.note: Serving since 1916; kulcha, dal and thalis in a cramped, much-loved heritage lane.

places.name: Bharawan Da Dhaba
places.note: Open since 1912; vegetarian institution famous for kulcha and overnight dal makhani.

places.name: All India Famous Kulcha Shop
places.note: Tandoor-fresh kulchas from morning until sold out; locals queue before noon.

food.name: Amritsari fish fry
food.desc: River fish marinated in ajwain, ginger and gram flour, then deep fried into golden nuggets and finished with chaat masala and lime.

places.name: Makhan Fish and Chicken Corner
places.note: The city benchmark for fish fry; busy late into the night.

places.name: Beera Chicken House
places.note: Long-running non-veg favourite for fish fry and tandoori chicken.

places.name: Surjit Food Plaza
places.note: Sit-down option on the main food street; fish fry plus tandoori platters.

food.name: Langar at the Golden Temple
food.desc: Free community meal of dal, sabzi, roti and kheer served round the clock to everyone; sit on the floor in rows and eat with pilgrims.

places.name: Guru Ka Langar, Sri Harmandir Sahib
places.note: Runs 24 hours daily, feeding tens of thousands; volunteers welcome in the dish hall.

places.name: Durgiana Temple langar
places.note: Quieter Hindu temple langar a short walk from the Golden Temple.

food.name: Amritsari chole
food.desc: Dark, tea-stained chickpeas simmered with anardana and garam masala, eaten with kulcha, bhature or plain rice.

places.name: Bharawan Da Dhaba
places.note: Chole bhature here set the city standard; always packed at lunch.

places.name: Kanha Sweets
places.note: Clean, family-friendly vegetarian hall doing chole bhature and chaat all day.

places.name: Brothers Dhaba
places.note: Neighbouring rival to Bharawan with the same vegetarian Punjabi repertoire.

food.name: Maa di dal (dal makhani)
food.desc: Black urad lentils simmered overnight on low coals with butter and cream until glossy and smoky; the richest thing on any Amritsari table.

places.name: Bharawan Da Dhaba
places.note: Its slow-cooked dal is as famous locally as the kulcha.

places.name: Kesar Da Dhaba
places.note: Century-old dhaba where the dal arrives swimming in white butter.

places.name: Surjit Food Plaza
places.note: Reliable version alongside the tandoori grills.

food.name: Jalebi and Punjabi mithai
food.desc: Coils of fermented batter fried and soaked in syrup, eaten hot for breakfast; alongside pinni, gur pareh and milk cake.

places.name: Gurdas Ram Jalebi Wala
places.area: Chowk Passian, near Kesar Da Dhaba
places.note: Decades-old stall frying jalebi to order from early morning.

places.name: Novelty Sweets
places.note: Old sweet house for pinni, patisa and boxed mithai to take home.

places.name: Kanha Sweets
places.note: Big counter of Punjabi sweets plus hot jalebi in the mornings.

food.name: Lassi
food.desc: Thick sweet or salted yoghurt drink served in a heavy steel tumbler under a lid of malai; the standard antidote to Punjabi heat.

places.name: Ahuja Milk Bhandar
places.area: Mai Sewa Bazaar, near Golden Temple
places.note: Famous for creamy lassi and paneer; a fixture of the temple lanes.

places.name: Gian Di Lassi
places.note: Legendary lassi topped with a thick layer of cream.

places.name: Kanha Sweets
places.note: Sit-down alternative with mango and sweet lassi year round.

food.name: Kanji and masala chai
food.desc: Tart winter kanji fermented from black carrots and mustard seed, and milky spiced chai brewed all day; both alcohol-free and everywhere.

places.name: Giani Tea Stall
places.note: Long-running chai stop that stays busy from dawn to late evening.

places.name: Hall Bazaar street stalls
places.note: Carts sell seasonal kanji in winter and chai the rest of the year.

places.name: Bharawan Da Dhaba
places.note: Strictly vegetarian and alcohol-free, with chai served with every meal.

landmarks: Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib)
Sikhism's holiest shrine floats gold-clad upon its sacred pool, welcoming all faiths to marvel, pray, and share langar meals served to 100,000 daily.
Jallianwala Bagh
The walled garden where British troops massacred hundreds of unarmed Indians in 1919, now a sobering memorial with bullet-scarred walls and eternal flame.
Wagah Border Ceremony
A gloriously theatrical daily flag-lowering ritual where high-kicking Indian and Pakistani border guards duel in choreographed pageantry before roaring crowds.
Akal Takht
The supreme seat of Sikh temporal authority facing the Golden Temple, founded by Guru Hargobind in 1606 as the throne of justice and community affairs.
Partition Museum
Housed in the historic Town Hall, the world's first museum devoted to the 1947 Partition tells its harrowing stories through survivor testimonies and artefacts.
Gobindgarh Fort
Maharaja Ranjit Singh's 18th-century fort reborn as a heritage theme park with coin museums, light shows, and Punjabi cultural performances.
Durgiana Temple
A Hindu twin of the Golden Temple, this silver-doored shrine to goddess Durga likewise rises gilded from the centre of a sacred tank.
Heritage Street and Hall Bazaar
The grand pedestrian corridor to the Golden Temple, lined with rosy colonial-Sikh facades, phulkari textile shops, and legendary Amritsari kulcha joints.
Maharaja Ranjit Singh Museum and Ram Bagh
The Lion of Punjab's summer palace set in Mughal-style gardens, displaying weapons, miniatures, and relics of the great Sikh empire.
Mata Lal Devi Temple
A delightfully labyrinthine cave-style temple of mirrored halls, tunnels, and shrines honouring the 20th-century female saint Lal Devi.

train.note: The Samjhauta Express to Lahore has been suspended since August 2019 and shows no sign of returning, so there is no working international train. Amritsar Junction is a 15-minute walk or short rickshaw ride from the Golden Temple, with Vande Bharat and Shatabdi services reaching Delhi in about six hours. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead.

bus.note: The Delhi-Lahore bus has also been suspended, so there is no scheduled international coach. Travellers still cross to Pakistan on foot at the Attari-Wagah border 30 km west, but only with a Pakistani visa arranged well in advance and the crossing is frequently closed - check before going. Domestic PRTC and Punjab Roadways buses leave the ISBT for Delhi, Chandigarh and Jammu; private coaches are on redBus (https://www.redbus.in/).

ferry.note: Amritsar is inland in Punjab with no navigable rivers or coast, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Harike Wetland Bird Sanctuary
half.blurb: One of North India's largest wetlands, formed at the confluence of two rivers and a major migratory bird stop.

half.name: Pul Kanjari
half.blurb: Restored 19th-century Sikh-era border village with a step-well and temple, once a resting point on the Lahore road.

half.name: Tarn Taran Sahib
half.blurb: Sikh pilgrimage town with the largest gurdwara tank in the world, built by Guru Arjan Dev.
